reuse.why: Routes getScheduledAmount through the new getRangedAmount, but the server call sites keep their own missing/number/range dispatch instead of calling the existing getScheduledAmount that already decides all three cases.

duplication.why: The range rule itself is defined once, but the pre-existing null/number/range ternary is left duplicated at four sites (and the op-based dispatch in the template) rather than collapsed onto getScheduledAmount.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount, where the tree keeps schedule amount logic.

scope.why: Only the ranged-amount rule, its call sites, a test and a release note.

maintainability.why: A future change to the range rule is made once, but any change touching missing or approximate amounts still has to be repeated at each site, and two exported functions now overlap.

bypasses_abstraction.where: forecast normalizeSchedule, schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and schedule-template.ts call getRangedAmount inside their own dispatch instead of getScheduledAmount.

one_place.where: shared/schedules.ts getRangedAmount is the single definition of the ranged rule, used by getScheduledAmount and by every server path (forecast, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, preview, budget template).
